# The plugin's version is the corpus content version, replacing whatever the source manifest stated —
# so the number on the plugin is the number of the data inside it.
.dist/plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json :: "version": "2.3.4"
.dist/plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json :: !"0.0.1"

# Every other key of the source manifest survives, including ones this tool has never heard of. The
# manifest is the corpus's own file and is edited rather than rebuilt.
.dist/plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json :: "displayName": "Example Libraries"
.dist/plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json :: "corpusRoot": "corpus"

# The trimmed component leaves the manifest with its files, so the plugin does not advertise a
# component that is not there.
.dist/plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json :: "path": "skills/glossary-lookup"
.dist/plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json :: !"skills/decision-lookup"

# `bundle.json` is where the plugin says what it holds and why anything is missing. Two corpora running
# one plugin name may ship different component sets, and this is what makes that answerable from
# outside.
.dist/plugin/bundle.json :: "bundleVersion": 1
.dist/plugin/bundle.json :: "corpusRoot": "corpus"
.dist/plugin/bundle.json :: "reason": "the export carries no adrs"

# It carries no timestamp and no commit. The export inside the plugin states both, and a second clock
# would be a second answer to one question.
.dist/plugin/bundle.json :: !"generatedAt"
.dist/plugin/bundle.json :: !"commit"

# The marketplace names the plugin as a path beneath itself.
.dist/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json :: "source": "./plugin"
.dist/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json :: "name": "example-libraries-local"
